audit.whatIsWrong: Rated 7.5/10 on a 44.83% win rate over 29 games.
audit.why: 45% is a losing lane but not a 7.5 — for comparison Sett and Sion sit near 33-35% on this champion. The difficulty scale collapses if a five-point deficit reads the same as a seventeen-point one.
audit.corrected: diffRating to 6.5/10 with the difficulty and final-rating lines following. diff (TRICKY) and tone stay as they are and remain accurate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The scaling story stops at 'his passive pulls soul fragments off you and dying minions to heal'.
audit.why: Riot on Ravenous Flock: 'Swain's ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health.' The permanent max-health growth is the whole reason a long lane against Swain gets worse rather than staying flat — every extended trade you take is a stat he keeps for the rest of the game. Also Vision of Empire is 5500 to 7500 range and reveals what it hits, so it collects fragments off you from across the map.
audit.corrected: Soul fragments heal AND permanently raise his max health; Vision of Empire reaches 5500 at rank 1 and reveals.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Nevermove as a normal forward skillshot — 'sails a bird out, and if you facecheck or push up he roots you'. It does not root on the way out.
audit.why: Riot: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer.' The root lands on the RETURN pass. That inverts the counterplay completely: dodging the throw does nothing, and standing still after it passes you is how you get caught. It also means the safe punch window starts once the wave has come home, not once it has left. Cooldown 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 850 range, and a landed root converts into a pull.
audit.corrected: Step out of the return path, not the throw. Punch after the wave has come back, and expect a pull if it lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Nevermove with no numbers, and phases[2] cites a 10-second cooldown.
audit.why: 10s is rank 5. At rank 1 it is 12s, which is the number that matters in the levels where this lane is decided. Vision of Empire is 22/21/20/19/18s and Death's Hand is 7/6/5/4/3s — the Q is nearly always up, so it is not something to wait out.
audit.corrected: Real ranks written into the cooldown block, phases[2], report[5] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three paired entries have descriptions that do not match their titles: dontsFull[1] is titled 'Fight inside Demonic Ascension without anti-heal' but described with the generic W-taunt line, dontsFull[2] is titled about his soul sustain but described with the same generic line, and breakdown.early claims 'your passive shield already blanks his chip'.
audit.why: The titles are the specific, correct advice for this matchup and the bodies underneath them are boilerplate about a different topic, so the two halves of each bullet contradict. And Galio has no passive shield — Colossal Smash is an empowered basic attack.
audit.corrected: Each body rewritten to actually explain its title; the phantom passive shield removed.

edits.before: Respect Swain at Levels 1-2 — his E, Nevermove, sails a bird out, and if you facecheck or push up he roots you in place for a free W (Vision of Empire) bomb and Q (Death's Hand) fan before your kit is online. Last-hit at the back of the wave and do not throw your slow E dash into his Nevermove range, because a landed root cancels your engage and hands him the trade plus a soul fragment for the heal. By Level 3 with Q-W-E you have a window: bait out the bird, channel Shield of Durand into the W bomb so the magic damage reduction eats it, then E-knockup him off the wave — but only once his root is down.
edits.after: Respect Swain at Levels 1-2 — Nevermove (E) sails a wave out and roots on the way BACK, not on the throw, so the counterplay is stepping out of its return path rather than dodging the launch. Get caught and he pulls you in for a free Vision of Empire bomb and Death's Hand fan before your kit is online. Last-hit at the back of the wave and never throw your slow E dash while his is still out. By Level 3 with Q-W-E you have a window: bait the bird, charge Shield of Durand into the W bomb so the magic reduction eats it, then E-knockup him off the wave once the return has passed.

edits.before: This is the grind where the lane is genuinely close if you play it clean: your W-taunt into E-knockup punishes any step-up, and your magic-amplified damage reduction does soak his W and Q. The problem is attrition — Swain doesn't burst, so there's no committed combo for your Shield of Durand to refund into a free kill; his passive pulls soul fragments off you and dying minions to heal, and every fight grows his stacks. Level 6 is your one real spike: Hero's Entrance lets you punish a Swain who walked up to farm, or just flag out and swing another lane while you're even here.
edits.after: This is the grind where the lane is genuinely close if you play it clean: your W-taunt into E-knockup punishes any step-up, and your magic-amplified reduction does soak his W and Q. The problem is attrition — Swain doesn't burst, so there's no committed combo for Shield of Durand to refund into a kill, and Ravenous Flock's soul fragments both heal him and permanently raise his maximum health, so every long trade makes him bigger for the rest of the game. Level 6 is your one real spike: Hero's Entrance punishes a Swain who walked up to farm, or flags out to swing another lane.

edits.before: You don't out-duel a 2+ item Swain — once Liandry's and Rylai's are online his R (Demonic Ascension) drain out-sustains your plateaued tank-AP damage, and a single landed Nevermove in a fight roots you inside his AOE. You won't die fast thanks to Shield of Durand, but you also can't kill him, and standing in his drain is exactly what he wants. Your job is the R flank: drop Hero's Entrance on his backline or peel a carry, because your value here is map presence and the taunt, never the 1v1.
edits.after: You don't out-duel a 2+ item Swain — Demonic Ascension stays up for as long as he keeps draining a champion, so without Grievous Wounds an extended fight has no ending you win. A single Nevermove return roots you inside the drain and he can pull you deeper into it. You won't die fast behind Shield of Durand, but you can't kill him either. Your job is the R flank: drop Hero's Entrance on his backline or peel a carry, because your value is map presence and the taunt, never the 1v1.

notes: The single biggest fix here is Nevermove's timing. The page had the player dodging the outgoing wave, which does nothing — Riot's text is explicit that the wave 'then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits', so the root is on the return pass and a Galio who sidesteps the throw and then stands still is doing exactly what Swain wants. Everything downstream of that (when to punch, when the dash is safe) was keyed off the wrong half of the ability. This full layer is otherwise the best-written one in the slice — someone had already given it real matchup-specific dos and donts — but three of those bullets had titles and bodies that did not match each other, with matchup-specific titles sitting on top of generic boilerplate bodies. Those pairings are fixed. UNVERIFIED and left alone: whether Galio's taunt or knockup interrupts Demonic Ascension, and whether the Nevermove pull is displacement Galio can be Flash-buffered out of — the kit's needsResearch is empty, meaning unknown. Galio's Justice Punch still carries the bogus derived 'terrain' flag that produced a 'Galio can cut your retreat' row for Swain in _missing-interactions.json; ignored.
